source_text: Martianus ait: Da nomina, ne poenae ipse succumbas. respondit Achatius: Ante tribunal ipse assisto, et nomen inquiris? an speras quod multos valeas vincere, quem ego solus extinguo? si cordi tuo nomina sunt, Achatius dicor, et si proprium nomen meum exploras, vocor Agathangelus, et Piso Troianorum episcopus, et Menander presbyter. fac iam quod placet. Martianus ait: Recipieris in carcerem, ut imperator gesta cognoscat et eius nutu quid de te agi debeat decernatur. lectis itaque omnibus gestis Decius imperator, alterationem iam redditae responsionis admirans, versus in risum est et Martiano praefecturam Pamphyliae mox dedit, Achatium vero vehementer admirans aestimationi propriae et legi suae reddidit. haec facta sunt a Martiano consulari, imperatore Decio, quarto kalendas Aprilis.
thought_title: Refusing to betray names and being sent back to prison
orientation: Martianus demands the names of those of the whole church, Achatius refuses to give them, and Martianus sends him back to prison until the emperor Decius decides.
pass_a_gloss: Martianus said: Give the names, lest you yourself sink under punishment. Achatius answered: I myself stand before the tribunal, and do you inquire for my name? Or do you hope that you will be strong enough to conquer many, when I alone extinguish you? If names are dear to your heart, I am called Achatius, and if you search out my proper name, I am called Agathangelus, and Piso bishop of the Trojans, and Menander presbyter. Do now what pleases you. Martianus said: You will be received back into prison, in order that the emperor may come to know the proceedings and in order that by his nod it may be decided what ought to be done concerning you. And so when all the proceedings had been read, Decius the emperor, wondering at the dispute of the answer already given, was turned to laughter and soon gave to Martianus the prefecture of Pamphylia, but admiring Achatius greatly he gave him back to his own judgment and his law. These things were done by Martianus the consular, when Decius was emperor, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April.

lemmas.gloss: heart as what is pleasing here
be received back into prison here
Kalends, first day of month here

choices.why: keeps literal force of extinguo and solus and relative quem, without softening to defeat

choices.english: if names are dear to your heart
choices.why: keeps dative cordi tuo as the seat of desire, not mere possession

choices.term: et Piso Troianorum episcopus, et Menander presbyter
choices.english: and Piso bishop of the Trojans, and Menander presbyter
choices.why: brief says syntax is uncertain whether further title or separate persons, so gloss leaves it unresolved

choices.term: aestimationi propriae et legi suae reddidit
choices.english: he gave him back to his own judgment and his law
choices.why: keeps reddidit as give back and aestimatio as judgment, without deciding whose law beyond suae

pass_b_english: Martianus said, "Give the names, so you yourself do not sink under the punishment." Achatius answered, "I stand before the tribunal myself, and you ask for my name? Do you hope to conquer many, when I alone extinguish you? If names are dear to your heart, I am called Achatius, and if you seek my proper name, I am called Agathangelus, and Piso bishop of the Trojans, and Menander presbyter. Do now what you please."
Martianus said, "You will be received back into prison, so the emperor may learn the proceedings and what should be done with you may be decided by his nod."

When all the proceedings had been read, the Emperor Decius wondered at the exchange of the answer already given and broke into laughter. He soon gave Martianus the prefecture of Pamphylia, but he greatly admired Achatius and gave him back to his own judgment and his law. This was done by Martianus the consular, under the Emperor Decius, four days before the Kalends of April.
notes: No damaged text is marked in the given source; the clause et Piso Troianorum episcopus, et Menander presbyter is syntactically ambiguous and is glossed without resolving whether it names the speaker further or other persons.
